Standard: Exposure to the acoustic noise environment for the stated life documented in engine tech data does not adversely affect the engine beyond the capability established in 7.2 standards, nor result in exceeding defined engine operating limits, detrimental permanent deformation, or damage when the engine is operated, at all thrust or power settings under installed or uninstalled steady state and transient conditions, IAW 7.3.1. Method of Compliance: Prior to entering flight test, verify the standard by the following method(s): Examination.
(1) Examine the definition of the installed and uninstalled acoustic noise environment used for final design analysis. The basis for the design curve is stated (e.g., test on actual system, correlation from another system). Analysis.
  (1) Structural analysis determines hardware tolerance to defined acoustic noise environment. Non-operating conditions are considered if applicable (e.g., supplementary propulsion systems, multi-mode propulsion systems). Test.
    (1) Lab test: Acoustic noise environment is characterized via measurement during engine test in a ground-based sea level test cell. Full power range is characterized (typical peak responses are at highest throttle setting). Instrumentation includes microphone arrays.
    (2) Lab test: Component durability is verified by measured dynamic stress or acceleration and via post-test inspection of engine-level durability test (AMT) hardware.
    (3) Ground test: Ground test is conducted to verify engine bay and external noise environment.
